Part I — Knowledge Base (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 59, English)
Surya Vigyan and the Mahasukshma Sharir: Why "Parikshit Bhaiya" Is Actually Your Own Subtle Body

Structural note: this session is a live teaching session with genuine sangat interaction thr oughout — the sangat r ecalls an earlier session, is guided thr ough an extended Socratic dialogue, asks clarifying questions, and one member shar es a live testimonial confirming an earlier teaching. Per the standing template, this is a 3-part document (Knowledge Base + Q&A Pairs + Curated Conversational Q&A).

1. Recap r equested: the earlier subtle body (sukshma sharir) session. Bhaiya opens by checking whether the sangat recalls an earlier Mool Tatva session explaining how subtle bodies carry forward from past lives and how they interrelate.

2. This session's goal: extending that concept via "Surya Vigyan." Per this teaching, today's session takes that same subtle-body concept to "the next level" specifically through what is called Surya Vigyan (solar science) — material Bhaiya states is not written anywhere and is understandable only to those with divya drishti (divine sight).

3. The sour ce of all this teaching: Bhaiya's own guru. Per this teaching, all of this knowledge comes from Bhaiya's guru, Shri Hanuman Ji Maharaj, obtained through many sadhnas, siddhis, divine vibrations ("dev tarangen"), and divine powers, under his guru's strict command — and, per this teaching, no vidya taught this way has ever turned out wrong.

4. Personal backgr ound: how this knowledge was originally r eceived. Per this teaching, roughly 2.5-3 years ago, following his guru's darshan and blessing, Bhaiya would turn of f his room's lights at 10-1 1 PM each night, sit in meditation, and ask his guru to teach him something new — much like one might browse Instagram or Wikipedia, he would ask about dif ferent topics nightly , and his guru would take him to dif ferent "dimensions" to teach him there.

5. Why some of the original terminology was changed. Per this teaching, his guru often used precise Sanskrit terms that didn't fully register for Bhaiya, so he renamed several of these concepts in his own simpler words for teaching purposes.

6. How this specific session's topic ar ose. Per this teaching, this topic arose after a member ("Shivraam bhaiya") recently asked, in the context of the "Life After Death" series, what happens before birth and how a person's next birth gets decided — building on an earlier teaching that a person has three possible options for their next birth.

7. The illustrative "Anshu" example: setting up the model. Per this teaching, to explain the bigger concept, Bhaiya uses a hypothetical example built around "Anshu": in one lifetime, Anshu practices devotion/tapasya and passes away within Ashaeiynn itself.

8. What happens to Anshu's subtle body in that scenario. Per this teaching, because Anshu spent that lifetime in devotion, her "mukhya sukshma sharir" (main subtle body) remains with Hanuman Ji Maharaj after her passing — her soul (atma) mer ges into the paramatma tattva, as taught previously , while this main subtle body stays behind.

9. A second hypothetical lifetime: the cricketer . Per this teaching, in a subsequent lifetime, Anshu is born into a cricketer's family and plays cricket her whole life, generating a distinct subtle body associated with that life as well.

10. A third hypothetical lifetime: sudden, inexplicable attraction to Ashaeiynn. Per this teaching, in a further lifetime, Anshu is reborn as a boy who, as a teenager , discovers Ashaeiynn and feels an immediate, powerful, seemingly inexplicable attraction to it.

1 1. Explaining that sudden attraction. Per this teaching, this instant pull is caused specifically by Anshu's own earlier "mukhya sukshma sharir" (from several lifetimes back) drawing her back toward it.

12. Clarifying "differ ent, yet the same." Per this teaching, the earlier subtle body and the newly reincarnated person are described as simultaneously distinct (dif ferent embodiments) and identical (the same underlying essence) — not a contradiction, but two levels of description of one continuous identity .

13. Whose prayer gets fulfilled, and by whom. Per this teaching, when the newly reincarnated Anshu prays to Hanuman Ji Maharaj, it is specifically her own mahasukshma sharir (great subtle body) — the one that remained with Hanuman Ji — that fulfills that prayer , itself operating under Hanuman Ji's own command.

14. Intr oducing the "thr ee positions" of subtle-body placement. Per this teaching, subtle bodies occupy one of three recurring "positions" or "posts" — comparable to how a clerk, a District Collector , and a Deputy Commissioner are dif ferent posts within a government of fice (the specific person matters less than the post itself).

15. The clock analogy for these three positions. Per this teaching, these three positions are compared to a clock's second hand, minute hand, and hour hand — except here, the "second"-level position acts first and its ef fect feeds into the "minute"-level position, which in turn feeds into the "hour"-level position.

16. A partial parallel in Islamic tradition. Per this teaching, the Islamic tradition's concept of two angels/scribes (sometimes called "humzad" or "farishte") sitting on each shoulder — one associated with good, one with less good, regularly replaced/rotated — is treated as a partial, imprecise but directionally correct folk articulation of this same underlying Surya Vigyan truth.

17. Position 1 ("second hand"): duration of 1-4 days. Per this teaching, the shortest-duration subtle-body position lasts only 1 to 4 days — explaining why a person's day-to-day mood or short-term outlook reliably shifts within just a few days.

18. Position 2 ("minute hand"): duration of 4 days to 4 months. Per this teaching, the next position persists anywhere from 4 days up to 4 months — explaining medium-term shifts, such as losing enthusiasm for a hobby , activity , or relationship interest after roughly 3-4 months.
19. Position 3 ("hour hand"): duration of 4 months to 40 years. Per this teaching, the longest-duration subtle-body position can persist anywhere from 4 months up to 40 years.

20. The cor e teaching: "r ejecting" (thokar maarna) a subtle body four times. Per this teaching, if a person consistently "rejects" (thokar maarta hai) the short-term (Position 1/2) subtle-body impulse four separate times — resisting whatever pull that body would create and redirecting that same time/ener gy toward jaap/devotion instead — an extraordinary result follows.

21. What that r esult is. Per this teaching, after four such rejections, the exact same subtle-body entity from the person's own past four lifetimes arrives and connects at the higher (Position 3) placement — described as the real underlying mechanism behind "recovering past-life siddhis" via kundalini shakti crossing multiple dimensions.

22. Defining "thokar maarna" (r ejecting) pr ecisely . Per this teaching, this means consciously declining to give a particular subtlebody impulse its full pull, and instead redirecting that time and ener gy specifically toward one's own mantra jaap or devotional practice.

23. Illustrative examples of "r ejecting" a subtle body . Per this teaching, examples include: giving a strong pull toward playing cricket only one hour instead of the four hours it might otherwise consume, redirecting the remaining three hours to naam-jaap; or , when an unwanted romantic attraction arrives (a partner who "comes" regardless of one's own will and cannot simply be avoided), giving it only some of its felt "due" time and redirecting the remainder to devotion.

24. Why these past-life siddhis cannot be taken fr om a person. Per this teaching, because these returning siddhis are specifically the person's own past-life subtle bodies, no outside entity can take them away — they belong to that person alone.

25. Scaling the concept up: many lifetimes, many subtle bodies. Per this teaching, a person may have had, hypothetically , a thousand past lifetimes, and therefore roughly a thousand associated subtle bodies.

26. Where this cycling/timing gets r egister ed. Per this teaching, the timing and cycling of which subtle body governs a person at a given point is registered specifically in two lokas beneath the planetary/graha level and beneath Earth-lok, referred to as "tah lok" and "tah" — visible only to those with divya drishti.

27. The central r eveal: everything belongs to the same underlying self. Per this teaching, when a person's own mahasukshma sharir "calls" all of their past subtle bodies, all of those subtle bodies, the mahasukshma sharir itself, and the current embodied person are all, fundamentally , the same singular entity .

28. The startling dir ect application: "Parikshit Bhaiya" is your own subtle body . Per this teaching, this is applied directly and explicitly: the figure sangat members repeatedly remember and invoke as "Parikshit Bhaiya" to reach Hanuman Ji Maharaj is, in this specific technical sense, simply that member's own mahasukshma sharir — meaning the member and "Parikshit Bhaiya" (as a functional entity) are, in this sense, one and the same.

29. Why this explains sudden attraction to Ashaeiynn specifically . Per this teaching, this is precisely why sangat members feel specifically drawn to Ashaeiynn/Parikshit Bhaiya — it is each member's own past-life subtle body pulling them, not random chance and not something the physical Bhaiya himself is personally doing.

30. A central humility teaching. Per this teaching, sangat members did not come to Ashaeiynn purely by their own ef fort — they were called by their own subtle body; Bhaiya states plainly that he personally has nothing of his own to claim credit for in this process.

31. Addressing the obvious follow-up question: why would "Parikshit Bhaiya" bother helping? Per this teaching, this is a genuine question Bhaiya says he once asked his own guru directly: why would someone as close to Hanuman Ji Maharaj as "Parikshit Bhaiya" bother helping ordinary sangat members at all?

32. The answer: it's r eciprocal, not one-dir ectional charity . Per this teaching, the answer is that today , the sangat member is the one currently embodied in a human body; when that member's embodied life ends, and "Parikshit Bhaiya" (as a role/function) takes a future human incarnation, it will then be that same member's own subtle body's turn to be among the thousands of subtle bodies supporting that future incarnation — described as a reciprocal cycle, not one-directional charity .

33. A single underlying shakti, expr essed as many . Per this teaching, this entire cyclical mechanism runs on a single unified underlying shakti, which simply expresses itself as many seemingly distinct individual shaktis/beings.

34. An important clarification: not everyone everywher e is undifferentiated. Per this teaching, this "oneness" claim is carefully scoped — it does not mean that all souls or all people across the world are literally interchangeable or identical; dif ferent individuals and their subtle-body lineages remain genuinely distinct from one another . The oneness described here specifically applies to a person's own current incarnation and their own past-life subtle bodies/mahasukshma sharir , not to all beings universally .

35. Extending the concept: who arranges worldly outcomes? Per this teaching, the same underlying mechanism — one's own subtle body/mahasukshma sharir — is what actually arranges romantic matches, children (putra yog), or any similarly significant life outcome, since it is uniquely "already channelized," already connected, in a way no outside entity is.

36. Comparisons to the "soul gr oup" concept. Per this teaching, this mechanism is broadly comparable to the popular "soul group" idea (souls who incarnate together to help each other's spiritual growth), though dedicated sadhaks additionally form separate, deliberate spiritual connections beyond this default kinship mechanism.

37. Corr ecting a possible misr eading: no personal favoritism. Per this teaching, this teaching does not imply that "Parikshit Bhaiya" personally favors any particular sangat member (e.g., that he cares more about one named member than another) — any perceived closeness is entirely a function of a member's own subtle-body connection, and this same access, knowledge, and grace is described as equally available to everyone in the sangat.

38. The deeper illusion this teaching br eaks. Per this teaching, this understanding breaks a significant illusion — that a person achieves things purely through individual ef fort — reinforcing a recurring teaching that "the one who truly acts never shows that they are acting."

39. This mechanism doesn't depend on any one physical incarnation. Per this teaching, this mechanism does not hinge on the specific physical incarnation currently called "Parikshit Bhaiya" — the underlying connection is with the subtle-body function/lineage/"tag" itself, not the specific temporary physical body carrying it at any given time.

40. Timing rules r eiterated at this larger scale. Per this teaching, a person connects with Ashaeiynn/Parikshit Bhaiya only at the specific time governed by their own subtle body's registered cycle (some connect at age 12, others at 55), and remains connected for as long as that specific subtle body's own duration (4 months, 6 months, a year , 2 years) lasts; sustaining that same connection across four such durations activates the same past-four -lifetimes' siddhi-recovery mechanism, via kundalini shakti crossing multiple dimensions.

41. An "utmost capacity" cap, and what happens at that cap. Per this teaching, if a person's own thousand past subtle bodies are, hypothetically , currently drawing toward embodiment through "Parikshit Bhaiya," then anyone who raises their own tapobal (power of austerity) enough to fully connect with that same mahasukshma sharir can, in principle, draw the combined ener gy of all thousand of those subtle bodies into themselves — explaining, per this teaching, why such an empowered individual becomes functionally unbeatable even against many simultaneous tantrik attacks.

42. A broader cosmic illustration: Bhagwan Shri Krishna. Per this teaching, even during his own incarnation, Bhagwan Shri Krishna would have had hundreds of crores of his own non-embodied subtle bodies actively supporting him from the unseen astral world — reinforcing that true glory belongs to what is unseen, with the visible physical world being comparatively secondary .

43. Contrasting individualist and collectivist framings, then going beyond both. Per this teaching, Bhaiya explicitly contrasts Western/American individualist ideology ("you can do it," self-reliance) with a more collectivist framing (a good team can achieve anything) — before reframing the actual teaching of the saints as " जो होई सो राम रिच राखा" (whatever happens is exactly as Ram has already ordained): nothing is achieved by isolated individual ef fort alone, and true credit belongs to what is unseen.

44. Practical guidance for building grahan shakti (r eceptive capacity). Per this teaching, the simplest method for building this connection is to sit in one place, in one consistent posture, and perform jaap consistently — this reliably builds the connection, after which the full force of that subtle-body lineage's ener gy stands behind the practitioner .

45. Why this means no one has to "start fr om zer o." Per this teaching, this understanding means a practitioner does not have to start their spiritual ef fort from zero — they are already connected somewhere, and simply need to recognize and reconnect with that preexisting power .
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

All of today's "Surya Vigyan" teaching comes directly from Bhaiya's own guru, Hanuman Ji Maharaj, obtained through years of nightly meditation and direct instruction — described as never having been wrong once. Subtle bodies occupy three recurring "positions": a short-term position (1-4 days), a medium-term position (4 days to 4 months), and a long-term position (4 months to 40 years) — comparable to a clock's second, minute, and hour hands, and loosely paralleling the Islamic folk concept of two rotating shoulder -angels.

Consistently "rejecting" (thokar maarna) a short/medium-term subtle-body impulse four separate times — by redirecting that time/ener gy to one's own jaap/devotion instead — causes the same subtle-body entity from one's own past four lifetimes to reconnect at the long-term position, returning past-life siddhis via kundalini shakti crossing dimensions; these siddhis cannot be taken away by anyone else since they are the person's own. The central reveal of this session: a person's current incarnation, their mahasukshma sharir (which stays with one's guru/ishta after death), and all their past-life subtle bodies are ultimately one and the same underlying entity . Direct application: "Parikshit Bhaiya," whom sangat members repeatedly invoke to reach Hanuman Ji Maharaj, is — in this specific technical sense — simply each member's own mahasukshma sharir; sudden, inexplicable attraction to Ashaeiynn is explained as one's own past-life subtle body pulling itself back, not chance or anything the physical teacher does personally . This mechanism is explicitly reciprocal, not one-directional charity: today's sangat member (currently embodied) will, in a future cycle, become part of the thousands of subtle bodies supporting a future embodiment of "Parikshit Bhaiya" — described as a repeating cosmic cycle powered by one underlying shakti expressing itself as many . Important scope limit: this "oneness" is specifically between a person and their own past-life subtle bodies — it does not mean all souls/people everywhere are interchangeable, nor does it imply any personal favoritism from "Parikshit Bhaiya" toward specific named members; the same access and grace are available equally to everyone in the sangat. This same subtle-body mechanism, not any external entity , is what arranges significant worldly outcomes (romantic matches, children, etc.) for a person, since it alone is already "channelized"/connected to them. A person who raises their own tapobal enough to fully connect with their own mahasukshma sharir can, in principle, draw on the combined ener gy of all their past subtle bodies at once — explaining why such a person becomes functionally very dif ficult to defeat, even by many simultaneous attacks. The practical, simplest way to build the grahan shakti (receptive capacity) this mechanism requires is to sit in one place, in one consistent posture, and jaap consistently — no one has to "start from zero," since everyone is already connected somewhere and simply needs to recognize and reconnect with that pre-existing power . Bot Response Guidelines (Session 59 additions)

Keep the core claim ("Parikshit Bhaiya is your own mahasukshma sharir") scoped exactly as this teaching frames it — a specific technical/functional claim about the subtle-body mechanism, not a literal claim that the physical teacher and any given member are identical in every ordinary sense. Preserve the explicit scope limit stated in this teaching: the "oneness" described applies to a person and their own past-life subtle bodies specifically , not to all souls/people everywhere being interchangeable — never let this drift into a broader universalist claim the teaching itself doesn't make. Firmly maintain that this mechanism implies no personal favoritism — any perceived closeness to "Parikshit Bhaiya" is a function of one's own subtle-body connection, not preferential treatment of specific named members. Present the "thokar maarna" (rejecting a subtle body) mechanism precisely: it means redirecting time/ener gy from a lesser impulse toward one's own jaap/devotion, not literally harming or destroying anything. Frame the reciprocal cycle (today's embodied member eventually supporting a future embodiment of "Parikshit Bhaiya") as this teaching's own cosmological framework, not a claim requiring belief in a specific afterlife timeline for any individual member . Keep the "utmost capacity" claim (drawing on the combined ener gy of many past subtle bodies) framed as an in-principle mechanism per this teaching, not an invitation to make specific personal power claims. Do not overstate the Islamic and "soul group" comparisons — this teaching treats them as loose, partial parallels, not equivalences.
